[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"System Design Tutorial: Publish-Subscribe Pattern & Topic Partitioning"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to Publish-Subscribe (Pub-Sub)"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Publish-Subscribe pattern is a messaging pattern where senders (publishers) of messages do not program the messages to be sent directly to specific receivers (subscribers). Instead, published messages are characterized into classes, without knowledge of what (if any) subscribers there may be."},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Decoupling: Publishers and subscribers are completely decoupled in terms of space, time, and synchronization."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scalability: Adding new publishers or subscribers does not affect existing components, making it ideal for distributed systems."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"The Bottleneck of Single-Topic Channels"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"In a basic Pub-Sub system, a topic is a single logical channel. However, as throughput increases, a single topic handled by a single broker becomes a performance bottleneck. All messages pass through one node, limiting CPU, memory, and network I/O."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Topic Partitioning for Scalability"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Topic partitioning splits a single logical topic into multiple physical partitions distributed across a cluster of brokers. This allows parallel processing, enabling high throughput and horizontal scalability."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Parallelism: Multiple consumers can read from different partitions of the same topic simultaneously."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ordering Guarantees: Ordering is typically preserved within a single partition, but not globally across partitions."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Partition Strategies"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"How do we decide which partition a message goes to? System designers use specific partitioning strategies:"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Round-Robin: Distributes messages evenly across all partitions to balance the load when order doesn't matter."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Key-Based Routing: Applies a hashing function to a message key (e.g., userId) to ensure all messages for that entity go to the exact same partition, preserving order."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Code Implementation Concept (Python)"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a conceptual representation of how key-based partitioning works in a distributed streaming platform like Apache Kafka."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"def get_partition(key, num_partitions):
    if not key:
        return random.randint(0, num_partitions - 1)
    return hash(key) % num_partitions

# Example usage:
partition_id = get_partition(key="user_12345", num_partitions=4)
print("Assigned to partition:", partition_id)"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Combining the Publish-Subscribe pattern with topic partitioning provides the foundational architecture for modern, high-throughput event-driven systems. By decoupling producers and consumers while scaling out data processing across partitions, architectures can handle millions of events per second reliably."}]
